newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF BRUGUERA V CHANG.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF BRUGUERA V CHANG.

text.p: Analysis of Monday's French Open men's singles fourth round match between second seed Michael Chang of the U.S. and 16th seed Sergi Bruguera of Spain, won 3-6 6-4 6-3 6-4 by Bruguera.

Bruguera made an uninspired start and Chang took advantage in the sixth game of the match, securing a break for a 4-2 lead. Serving for the set, the American showed impressive coolness, wrong-footing his opponent for 15-0, producing a timely ace for 40-0 and putting Bruguera under pressure on his first set point to ensure the Spaniard hit a service return wide.

Chang continued his good work by breaking immediately for a 2-0 lead, only to allow errors to erode his promising position. Bruguera pulled back to 2-2 when Chang missed an attempted winner by a whisker, but neither player could hold their next service games as the contest grew increasingly scrappy. Finally it was Bruguera who pulled himself together to take the set by breaking Chang for a third time.

Bruguera jumped into a 3-0 lead, only to be hauled back by Chang to 3-3 despite a bullet backhand in the sixth game to rival anything seen in the match. Yet again, though, Chang could not take several chances and was broken again in the eighth game as Bruguera took the next three games in a row.

Neither player's serve was proving a frightening proposition and Chang wasted two break points in the second game which would have given him a 2-0 lead. Instead, there was a break apiece in the third and fourth games and several more of the disputed calls which riddled the action before Bruguera broke for 5-4 and completed the job in two hours 54 minutes.
